note.note:
Consult Summary:  
30-year-old postpartum female (4 weeks post-C-section) presenting with sudden onset shortness of breath at rest for one hour, associated with tachycardia, recent cough, and chest soreness; clinical concern for pulmonary embolism prompting urgent hospital evaluation.  

History:  
- Patient reports sudden onset shortness of breath while sitting watching TV, lasting about one hour prior to consult.  
- Developed cough starting the day before; cough is non-productive, no sputum.  
- Denies chest pain except soreness on deep inspiration; tenderness noted over C-section scar area.  
- Palpitations described as feeling heart "really going."  
- No previous episodes of similar shortness of breath.  
- No fever, chills, or systemic symptoms reported.  
- No swelling or pain in legs reported.  
- Recent cesarean section performed 4 weeks ago.  
- No other chronic medical conditions.  
- Experienced frequent coughs and colds historically but none in recent months before current symptoms.  
- Allergic to ibuprofen; reaction details not specified.  

Past Medical History:  
- No chronic illnesses reported.  
- Recent surgery: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago, recovering with ongoing scar tenderness.  

Medications:  
- Codeine for post-C-section pain relief, used fairly regularly but not taken in the past week; dose/route/frequency not documented.  

Allergies:  
- Ibuprofen (reaction unspecified).  

Social History:  
- Lives at home with baby; partner currently at work, patient alone with baby.  
- Employment or smoking/alcohol/substance use not detailed.  
- Financial or lifestyle factors not mentioned.  

Family History:  
- Mother has history of venous clots in legs (venous thromboembolism).  

Physical Examination:  
- Vital signs not formally recorded; patient palpated own pulse at ~180 bpm (30 beats in 10 seconds).  
- Chest tenderness notably related to C-section scar and on deep inspiration.  
- No other examination findings recorded.  

Investigations:  
- No laboratory or imaging results available at time of consult.  

Assessment & Plan:  

Overall Impression:  
- High suspicion for pulmonary embolism given sudden onset dyspnea at rest, tachycardia, recent C-section (major thrombosis risk), pleuritic chest soreness, and positive family history of venous thromboembolism.  

DDx Integration:  
- Pulmonary Embolism: Supported by postpartum status, sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, chest soreness worsened by inspiration, and positive family history; no hypoxia or leg swelling reported but these findings may be absent early.  
- Respiratory Infection (Bronchitis/Pneumonia): Recent cough supports infectious etiology but absence of fever, sputum, or progressive symptoms make this less likely.  
- Postpartum Anxiety/Panic Attack: Palpitations and tachycardia present with reported stress but sudden onset and clinical context necessitate exclusion of organic causes first.  

Issue 1: Pulmonary Embolism (High suspicion)  
- Given recent C-section and acute presentation, PE is the leading concern.  
- Immediate referral to hospital for urgent assessment, including imaging and blood tests (e.g., D-dimer, CT pulmonary angiography).  
- Patient advised to attend emergency services promptly with baby; avoided taking codeine to prevent respiratory compromise.  
- Safety netting: advised regarding symptoms worsening, chest pain, leg swelling, or syncope requiring emergency attention.  

Issue 2: Respiratory Infection  
- New onset cough may represent early bronchitis or pneumonia.  
- Further evaluation in hospital setting to identify infection and initiate antibiotics if indicated.  

Issue 3: Postpartum Anxiety/Stress related tachycardia  
- Acknowledge presence of stress and palpitations as possible contributing factors.  
- Will be reconsidered after organic causes have been excluded.  

General Plan:  
- Urgent hospital evaluation prioritized to exclude life-threatening causes.  
- Avoidance of codeine until assessment completed.  
- Monitor for worsening symptoms or new signs.  

Quality checks:  
- Allergies documented but reaction to ibuprofen unspecified; further clarification recommended.  
- Medication dosing/frequency not fully documented for codeine.  
- No vital signs formally recorded beyond patient self-palpated heart rate.  
- No physical examination findings other than patient-reported tenderness available.  
- No investigations performed at time of consult.  
- Transcript clear; no audio quality issues noted.  
- DDx consistent with transcript; no conflicts noted.
